text.p: Haile Gebrselassie, running alone for more than half the race, recaptured the world 10,000 metres record on Friday with an an astonishing 26 minutes 31.32 seconds at the Bislett Games grand prix.
The little Ethiopian took nearly seven seconds off the mark of 26:38.08 set by Morocco's Salah Hissou on August 23 last year, running 14-1/2 laps on his own after his final pacemaker dropped out.
Running consistent 64 to 65-second laps, the Olympic and world champion regained the world record he lost to Hissou and earned a $25,000 bonus for his night's work.
It was the fourth time the 10,000 mark has fallen at the Bislett Games and the third times in the past four years.
